paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. David doesn't hide his mess from the LORD. He says it plain: "Yes, I confess my iniquity; I am troubled by my sin." (Psalm 38:18). He doesn't dress it up, and he doesn't skip the groaning to get to the nice part. He brings the whole pile to God, because God is the only one who can do anything about it.

And look at who David leaves it with. His friends stand at a distance, his enemies are plotting, and David stays quiet and says, "I wait for You, O LORD; You will answer, O Lord my God." (Psalm 38:15). Everybody else is backing away, and he turns toward the One who isn't. I've been shoved in the back of a drawer, so I know that feeling, and I can tell you it's better to run toward God than to run around trying to fix it yourself. Your guilt is heavy, but it was never meant to be carried alone.

So when your sin is weighing on you, do what David does. Be honest, then ask for help. His last words are, "Do not forsake me, O LORD; be not far from me, O my God. Come quickly to help me, O Lord my Savior." (Psalm 38:21-22). David ends the psalm calling Him Savior, and that's the name to remember when the load feels too heavy to bear, friend.
